Let
\[
h(s)=-g'(s).
\]
Since
\[
\bigl(s^5|g'|g'\bigr)'=-s^5g^5<0
\]
and \(s^5|g'|g'\to0\) as \(s\to0^+\), we get \(s^5|g'|g'<0\), hence \(g'<0\) and \(h>0\) for \(s>0\). Thus
\[
(s^5h^2)'=s^5g^5.
\]

Define
\[
P(s)=\frac{s^6g^6}{6}-s^5gh^2+\frac23s^6h^3.
\]
Differentiating and using \((s^5h^2)'=s^5g^5\) gives \(P'(s)=0\). Also \(P(s)\to0\) as \(s\to0^+\), so \(P\equiv0\).

Now set
\[
u(s)=sg(s),\qquad r(s)=\frac{sh(s)}{g(s)}.
\]
Then \(u>0\), \(0<r<3/2\), and \(P=0\) becomes
\[
u^3=2r^2(3-2r).
\]
Writing \(t=\log s\), one has
\[
\frac{d\log u}{dt}=1-r.
\]
Also, from \((s^5h^2)'=s^5g^5\), the variable \(r\) satisfies
\[
\frac{dr}{dt}=\frac12r(3-2r).
\]
Solving,
\[
r(s)=\frac{\frac32 C s^{3/2}}{1+C s^{3/2}}.
\]
Near \(0\),
\[
h(s)^2=s^{-5}\int_0^s t^5g(t)^5\,dt\sim \frac{s}{6},
\]
so \(r(s)\sim s^{3/2}/\sqrt6\). Therefore
\[
\frac32 C=\frac1{\sqrt6},
\qquad
C=\sqrt{\frac{2}{27}}.
\]
Finally,
\[
\frac{d\log g}{dt}=-r
\]
gives
\[
g(s)=\frac{1}{1+\sqrt{\frac{2}{27}}s^{3/2}},
\]
using \(g(0)=1\). Since \(g(s)=f(e^s)\), with \(s=\log x\),

\[
\boxed{f(x)=\frac{1}{1+\sqrt{\frac{2}{27}}(\log x)^{3/2}}}.
\]
